prompt:
Normalize the one contact record embedded in the user’s note. Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys "name", "phone", "email", "company", and "country". Every value must be a string or JSON null. No prose, fences, or extra keys.

First isolate the record block. Its lines have contact labels and values separated by a colon, equals sign, or tab; labels can vary and lines can appear in any order. Split each line at its label separator, not at punctuation inside the value. Ignore surrounding notes and signatures. Trim values and collapse each internal whitespace run to one space. An absent or empty value, or an exact case-insensitive match for -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, or TBD, is missing. Missing fields are null, except for the country rule below.

Assign before formatting:
- Reserve the country line for country. For other record lines, a value containing @ belongs to email regardless of its label. A value that, after removing a leading tel: and a trailing extension, contains at least seven digits and only digits, spaces, or + - ( ) . / belongs to phone regardless of its label. Check for these assignments even if the phone and email labels are reversed.
- Use the name and company labels for the remaining name and company values, but swap their roles if the name-labeled value ends in a legal suffix from the list below and the company-labeled value does not. Test before stripping the suffix.

Format the assigned values:
- Name: if there is a comma, split at the first comma and move the right-hand part before the left-hand part. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, or Prof, case-insensitively, with or without a dot. For each space- or hyphen-separated part, uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; do not transliterate.
- Company: remove the trailing legal suffix and any optional comma immediately before it, then trim. Match the complete suffix case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character of each space-separated word and lowercase the rest.
- Email: remove the mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets, even when one wrapper encloses the other. Lowercase the address. Copy the remaining characters faithfully: preserve the spelling, punctuation, and diacritics of both the local part and domain. Do not reconstruct either from another field.
- Country line: map an English, Swedish, or German country name, ISO alpha-2 or alpha-3 code, or common alias, case-insensitively, to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. In particular: UK and Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA and U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.
- Phone: remove a leading tel: and any trailing extension of the form ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12, or extension 12, where 12 represents extension digits. After ignoring the leading tel: and an opening parenthesis, a leading + or 00 marks an international number. For an international number, remove the literal optional-trunk marker (0) before removing punctuation, convert the leading 00 to + if present, and remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses. Keep the written calling code unchanged. For a national number, remove formatting punctuation and spaces, drop one leading trunk 0, and prepend + and the calling code of the normalized country from the country line. If there is no country, a national phone is null. All non-null phones are E.164: + followed only by calling-code and national-number digits.

Resolve country last: if the country line is missing, empty, or a placeholder and the phone is international, set country to the ISO alpha-2 code of the country uniquely identified by the calling code. If the calling code is shared (such as +1 or +7), leave country null. This is the only exception to the missing-field rule. When an explicit country and an international phone disagree, retain both the country from the line and the calling code from the phone. Do not infer anything else from notes, signatures, email domains, or company suffixes.

Before emitting the object, check that the email matches the source after only the specified cleanup, that the country exception was applied when appropriate, and that all five keys are present.
